extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing. The benchmark addresses four key weaknesses of existing benchmarks: lack of voice personalization evaluation, limited focus on hands-free interaction, neglect of various audio contexts, and insufficient multi-modal (vision+audio) integration assessment.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.publisher: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK
extraction.inLanguage: English (with 5 Chinese roles in the role-play task)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Test data was collected by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 (later mentioned as 47) source datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. For voice personalization, texts from RoleBench were used with 100 distinct roles and three representative audio clips per role. Text instructions were converted to audio using three TTS models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B), evaluated with UTMOS (regenerating clips scoring below 3.8), and transcribed with Whisper for quality verification via word error rate.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources include 47 datasets: MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, BIG-Bench Hard, Clotho, SLURP, VoiceBench, MTJ-Jamendo, JL Corpus, MELD, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, CoVoST 2, LibriSpeech, VocalSound, VoxCeleb1, MUSIA-AVQA, FoR, SpeechInstructBench, IEMOCAP, FollowBench, SpokenWOZ, TUT2017, AVQA, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, STORAL, Clotho-AQA, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, MyST.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text preprocessing for TTS synthesis: (1) Image references replaced with descriptive phrases (e.g., '<image1>' to 'as shown in the first image'); (2) Text rewriting using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to make text more suitable for TTS (e.g., 'OC=2rsin(π)' converted to 'O C equals two r times sine of pi'); (3) Multiple-choice questions rephrased for readability.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Four-stage curation: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance with manual review; (2) Validation excluding incomplete/unsuitable instances (corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, incorrect answers), with approximately 10% discarded; (3) Categorization into 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Balanced sampling across categories. Speech synthesis used UTMOS Strong with regeneration threshold of 3.8, followed by Whisper-Large-v3 transcription and selection of audio with lowest word error rate.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Task categorization primarily based on source metadata from original datasets. Human evaluation was performed on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B's responses (1050 examples) for validation. Error analysis involved manual examination of 593 error cases categorized into error types (Context Loss, Perception Errors, Requirement Deviation, etc.).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom lightweight web-based curation tool with inline audio players, image viewers, transcripts, and multiple-choice display.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between automated gpt-oss-20b evaluation and human judgments showed Pearson correlations from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92) and agreement rates mostly above 90% (overall 96.1%). Evaluation stability verified through 10 repeated runs showing low variance.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: UTMOS (Saeki et al., 2022) for speech quality; Whisper-Large-v3 (Radford et al., 2022) for transcription; gpt-oss-20b (OpenAI et al., 2025) for content quality evaluation; emotion2vec (Ma et al., 2023) for emotion probability detection; Wespeaker (Wang et al., 2023b; 2024c) for speaker similarity; F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B for speech synthesis; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for text rewriting.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code and data will be released publicly. The authors state they will release both the dataset and evaluation code. They also mention maintaining a data governance process for auditing and removal, reserving the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes voice/speaker characteristics (timbre) of 100 distinct roles with audio clips, emotional expressions (7 emotions: angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, surprised), and speech from various speakers across source datasets. Includes language demographics (primarily English with 5 Chinese roles).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to drive development of next-generation multimodal voice assistants for applications in healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive industries. Authors note risks of misuse including identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud through voice cloning. Mitigation measures include prohibiting training models to reproduce identifiable speakers without consent, requiring consent gating and watermarking, and providing safety cards describing acceptable use and known risks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases from source data and design choices. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources which may not reflect full richness of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. The dataset is predominantly monolingual (English) which may not capture global variability.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: (1) Limited diversity - mostly English with only 5 Chinese roles; (2) Limited model coverage - primarily open-source models with only one proprietary system (GPT-4o-Audio); (3) Evaluation methodology relies on automated GPT-based scoring which may introduce noise and bias; (4) Potential biases from source data and design choices; (5) Gaps in task coverage - video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond scope; (6) Offline static evaluation that doesn't capture latency constraints, continuous listening, or real-time interaction factors.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for evaluating/testing voice assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing abilities. Not intended for training models for cheating. Researchers should use this dataset to better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies. Use cases include benchmarking AI assistants for audio understanding, speech generation quality, voice personalization, hands-free interaction, multimodal integration, safety alignment, and robustness.
